output.brief: The rejects are not caused by the new operators or by the Arnholt resin on its own. The problem is wet Arnholt resin being dried in dryer D5, which has been degraded since late July (dew point about -16 to -19 C instead of -40 C). Evidence: all second-shift VX comes from Press 5. The new hires reject at the same rate as experienced operators (about 9.9% vs 10.3% on Arnholt; 0.9% on Quillan). Arnholt run on Press 7 with the good dryer D7 is at 0.8%. The same Arnholt lot gave 10.4% rejects through D5 but 0.8% when dried in a portable dryer at -40 C. I am fairly confident in this. Two gaps remain: Arnholt has only been stored in the north annex, so the storage effect is not separated from the supplier, and the sampling is small. This week: repair D5 and restore its original alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until it is verified. Add a moisture check at the press throat for every resin lot. Do not put the six operators on improvement plans. Moving stock out of the annex can wait until its effect is measured.
